transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-06-06 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 mins
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Evan Torres (Horizon Labs - Procurement), Dr. Sofia Reyes (Horizon Labs - Data Privacy), Marcus Lee (Horizon Labs - CTO), Aisha Nadeem (Horizon Labs - FinOps)

Summary (auto): Align on procurement requirements, agree pilot on Dedicated, DPA redlines next week, confirm SLA targets and KMS approach.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining i think we have most folks on the line, quick intro from redwood side - maya here, priya and liam with me.
[00:22] Evan Torres: hey thanks, Evan from procurement, i'll be shepherding the MSA/DPA thru our legal queue.
[00:30] Marcus Lee: Marcus here, CTO, i'll focus on the tech constraints — latency, keys, and residency.
[00:38] Dr. Sofia Reyes: Sofia, privacy lead, hi. want to be sure we cover retention and audit logs.
[00:45] Maya Chen: perfect, goal for today is to align procurement + security + eng on a narrow pilot and pricing lock so you can get committee approval. we'll surface open DPA items and SLAs.
[01:10] Priya Kapoor: quick agenda, we'll hit the pilot topology (dedicated vs hosted), SLA targets (p95/p99), KMS options (bring-your-own key/hsm), and then procurement asks.
[01:35] Aisha Nadeem: from finops we need a cost readout and an estimate for peak egress fees.
[01:42] Liam O'Connor: noted, we'll show a sample billing run for the pilot.

[05:00] Evan Torres: first re: contract - our legal prefers minimal DPA exceptions, SOC2 plus iso is a baseline, and we may request a data processing role clarity for subprocessor list.
[05:30] Maya Chen: that's expected. we can provide our SOC 2 report and an up-to-date subprocessor list. for DPA redlines - priya will run a redline and include data flow.
[06:00] Dr. Sofia Reyes: important: logs must be retained for 180 days for auditing, but access controls need separation. also looking for field-level masking options for pii.
[06:24] Priya Kapoor: we support configurable retention windows, and we can enable masking at ingestion for sensitive attributes; will note configuration in runbook.

[09:12] Marcus Lee: on KMS, can you confirm HSM-backed keys? we can't ship keys to a third party.
[09:22] Maya Chen: yes, we support customer-managed keys via Cloud KMS integrations and offer HSM-backed options depending on your provider. there are a couple of notes around egress and keying during migrations.
[09:45] Marcus Lee: migration... meaning if we later move on-prem? how are KV caches handled?
[09:53] Priya Kapoor: good question, KV cache persists in the serving layer; during migration we have a data export path, but for pilot we recommend Dedicated in your VPC so keys never leave your control.

[12:05] Evan Torres: procurement will need a price lock for 90 days after we sign so we can get committee approval. what's typical?
[12:16] Maya Chen: we can do a 90-day price protection for pilot pricing on Dedicated capacity. standard renewals follow the published rate card but we'll list the lock in the SOW.
[12:32] Aisha Nadeem: ok great, and can you break out egress vs tokens? we need to model worst-case.
[12:40] Liam O'Connor: yes, we'll send a sample spreadsheet showing token-based compute, storage, and egress assumptions.

[15:00] Dr. Sofia Reyes: one more on SLA - we need p99 latency targets for inference under the pilot and an error budget definition. what's realistic?
[15:12] Priya Kapoor: for the model profile you picked (2B context), typical p99 is ~350ms under Dedicated with continuous batching; we can set an SLO at 500ms p99 with fallbacks to a lower-cost variant. error budget and measurement are per-route, we'll instrument traces to measure.
[15:35] Marcus Lee: fallback sounds good — we need graceful degradation rather than failed responses.

[18:20] Maya Chen: on the MSA side, do you have any dealbreakers? i.e., egress fee caps, indemnity limits, or required escrow?
[18:31] Evan Torres: indemnity needs to be mutual and we might ask for a small escrow on outage credits if we exceed more than two SLA misses in a quarter.
[18:43] Maya Chen: crediting for SLA misses is standard, we can propose a formula in the SOW. escrow is less common but we can discuss.

[21:05] Dr. Sofia Reyes: about subprocessing — we need a list of infra partners (cloud regions) and confirmation of no model logging of raw user transcripts without opt-in.
[21:22] Priya Kapoor: confirmed — default is no raw transcript retention beyond configured logs; we can include explicit language for no training on customer data and provide the subprocessor inventory.

[24:00] Aisha Nadeem: budgeting question - if pilot exceeds commit we need per-request caps; can we put a soft cap and alerts?
[24:10] Liam O'Connor: yes, we support quotas and billing alerts; we can set soft caps and an overage approval flow.

[27:00] Evan Torres: how long to get the DPA redline back? our legal is quick but needs a clear owner.
[27:10] Maya Chen: priya will own the DPA redline, i'll support commercial points. target turnaround by 2025-06-10.

[30:30] Marcus Lee: technical checklist for pilot — network peering, KMS integration, model pinning to version, and performance baseline. can redwood provide a runbook?
[30:45] Priya Kapoor: yes we'll provide a 1pager runbook and a runbook repo with a checklist for peering, keys, sample curl commands, and monitoring dashboards.

[33:00] Dr. Sofia Reyes: monitoring — need audit logs to be immutable and exportable to our SIEM.
[33:12] Priya Kapoor: we have immutable buckets for audit traces and can stream logs to your SIEM via secure forwarder.

[36:00] Maya Chen: quick note on competitors: we've seen customers tradeoff Anthropic's cost profile with open models; sometimes teams consider building in-house. main win for us is operational consistency and cost controls.
[36:20] Evan Torres: good to know. procurement will do an apples-to-apples cost comparison.

[38:50] Aisha Nadeem: milestone timeline for procurement: decision committee 2025-06-20. we need deliverables by 2025-06-13 to make that.
[39:00] Maya Chen: understood — high-priority items: DPA redline by 6/10, pricing SOW and spreadsheet by 6/09, pilot kickoff scheduling by 6/16.

[42:00] Marcus Lee: any compliance add-ons for FedRAMP or specific healthcare regs?
[42:12] Priya Kapoor: currently SOC2/ISO; FedRAMP is a longer program. for healthcare we support HIPAA on private deployments and can scope BAAs in the DPA.

[45:10] Evan Torres: ok let's talk credits - if SLA is missed twice we want an automatic credit formula rather than case-by-case.
[45:22] Maya Chen: we can propose a tiered credit system in the SOW — automatic credits applied based on p99 breach thresholds. we'll include examples.

[48:30] Dr. Sofia Reyes: small ask — can you add a clause that Redwood won't use customer prompts/data for model training?
[48:42] Priya Kapoor: yes, we'll add explicit language and an attestation to the DPA; we already have a no-training-default for enterprise pods.

[50:00] Maya Chen: recap and next steps: priya owns DPA redline (due 6/10), liam will send pilot billing spreadsheet (due 6/09), evan will circulate procurement checklist (due 6/13). we'll schedule the pilot kickoff week of 6/16.
[50:25] Evan Torres: sounds good, i'll block time for procurement to review.
[50:35] Marcus Lee: we'll review the runbook and share any infra blockers by 6/09.
[51:00] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to SOC2, subprocessor list, and the sample billing model.

End of transcript.
